title: How Much Does a Trip Actually Cost? Realistic Daily Budgets by Destination
metaDescription: Realistic daily travel budgets for popular destinations across three tiers — backpacker, mid-range and comfortable — covering accommodation, food and transport.
excerpt: Not what a destination could cost, but what it does cost — per person, per day, at three honest spending levels.
author: Trypinn Team
content:
"How much do I need?" is the first real question of any trip, and the internet answers it badly — either with fantasy backpacker figures that assume you never take a taxi, or with luxury estimates that assume you never eat anywhere ordinary.

What follows is a set of realistic **per-person, per-day** ranges covering accommodation, food, local transport and everyday activities. They exclude international flights and visa costs, which are one-off and route-dependent.

Three tiers throughout:

- **Budget** — hostel dorm or basic guesthouse, street and local food, public transport, mostly free attractions
- **Mid-range** — a decent private room or three-star hotel, a mix of local and sit-down restaurants, occasional taxis, paid attractions
- **Comfortable** — a good four-star hotel or quality apartment, restaurants by choice rather than by price, taxis without thinking, tours and experiences

## Southeast Asia

The best value in the world for what you get.

- **Vietnam** — Budget $25–35 · Mid $50–80 · Comfortable $120–180
- **Thailand** — Budget $30–40 · Mid $60–100 · Comfortable $150–250. Bangkok and the islands sit at the top of each band; the north is cheaper
- **Indonesia (Bali)** — Budget $25–40 · Mid $60–100 · Comfortable $150–300. Canggu and Seminyak now cost multiples of Ubud
- **Cambodia and Laos** — Budget $25–35 · Mid $50–75 · Comfortable $110–160
- **Malaysia** — Budget $30–40 · Mid $60–90 · Comfortable $130–200
- **Philippines** — Budget $30–45 · Mid $65–100 · Comfortable $140–220. Island transfers add up fast and are the item people forget

![Budget Travel travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583417319070-4a69db38a482?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## South Asia

- **India** — Budget $20–30 · Mid $45–75 · Comfortable $120–250. Enormous internal variation: Goa in peak season and Mumbai cost several times rural Madhya Pradesh
- **Sri Lanka** — Budget $25–35 · Mid $55–85 · Comfortable $130–200
- **Nepal** — Budget $20–30 · Mid $45–70 · Comfortable $100–160, plus trekking permits and guide costs on top for the Himalaya
- **Bhutan** — effectively a fixed floor because of the Sustainable Development Fee, which changes the arithmetic entirely

## East Asia

- **Japan** — Budget $60–85 · Mid $120–180 · Comfortable $250–400. Cheaper than its reputation for food, more expensive for accommodation. A rail pass is worth the maths only if you are moving frequently
- **South Korea** — Budget $50–70 · Mid $100–150 · Comfortable $200–300
- **Taiwan** — Budget $40–55 · Mid $80–120 · Comfortable $170–250. Arguably the best value in the region
- **China** — Budget $35–50 · Mid $80–130 · Comfortable $180–300

## Europe

The widest internal spread of any region.

**Western and Northern Europe**
- **Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Denmark** — Budget $90–130 · Mid $180–280 · Comfortable $350–550
- **UK, France, Germany, Netherlands, Austria** — Budget $70–100 · Mid $140–220 · Comfortable $280–450
- **Italy and Spain** — Budget $60–85 · Mid $120–180 · Comfortable $250–400

**Central, Eastern and the Balkans** — where the value is
- **Portugal and Greece** — Budget $50–70 · Mid $100–160 · Comfortable $200–330
- **Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania** — Budget $45–60 · Mid $85–130 · Comfortable $170–280
- **Albania, Montenegro, Bosnia, North Macedonia** — Budget $35–50 · Mid $70–110 · Comfortable $150–250
- **Georgia and Armenia** — Budget $30–45 · Mid $65–100 · Comfortable $140–230

![Budget Travel travel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1531737212413-667205e1cda7?fm=webp&w=1200&q=60)

## The Americas

- **United States** — Budget $90–130 · Mid $180–280 · Comfortable $350–600. Cities and national park gateways at the top; add a rental car almost everywhere outside major metros
- **Canada** — Budget $80–115 · Mid $160–250 · Comfortable $320–500
- **Mexico** — Budget $40–55 · Mid $85–140 · Comfortable $200–350. Resort areas cost double the interior
- **Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador** — Budget $30–45 · Mid $70–110 · Comfortable $150–260
- **Argentina and Chile** — Budget $40–60 · Mid $85–140 · Comfortable $180–320. Argentina's pricing has been unusually volatile; verify recent figures
- **Brazil** — Budget $40–60 · Mid $90–150 · Comfortable $200–350
- **Costa Rica** — Budget $55–75 · Mid $110–170 · Comfortable $250–400. Pricier than its neighbours

## Africa and the Middle East

- **Morocco and Egypt** — Budget $30–45 · Mid $70–110 · Comfortable $160–280
- **South Africa** — Budget $40–55 · Mid $80–130 · Comfortable $180–320, excellent value at the top end
- **Kenya and Tanzania** — Budget $45–65 · Mid $100–160 outside parks · safaris are a separate line item at $200–700 per person per day
- **UAE** — Budget $60–85 · Mid $130–200 · Comfortable $300–600
- **Jordan** — Budget $50–70 · Mid $100–150 · Comfortable $220–380
- **Turkey** — Budget $35–50 · Mid $75–120 · Comfortable $160–300

## Oceania

- **Australia and New Zealand** — Budget $75–105 · Mid $150–230 · Comfortable $300–500. A campervan changes the arithmetic substantially on a long trip
- **Fiji and the Pacific** — Budget $60–90 · Mid $150–250 · Comfortable $400+, dominated by resort pricing and inter-island flights

## The Line Items People Forget

Whatever tier you choose, these sit outside the daily figure and routinely blow budgets:

- **Internal flights and long-distance trains** — often the largest single in-country cost
- **Multi-day tours, safaris, treks and dive courses**
- **Entry fees at major sites** — a full day of museums in a European capital is easily $60–100
- **Airport transfers**, at both ends, in every city
- **Laundry** on trips longer than a week
- **Data and eSIM**
- **A contingency of 10–15%**. Not optional. Trips have weather, illness, missed connections and one genuinely great opportunity you did not plan for

## How to Use These Numbers

Pick your tier honestly — not the one you aspire to, the one matching how you actually travel. Multiply by nights, add the forgotten items above, add flights, add contingency.

Then, and this matters for groups: **share the number before anyone books.** The most common source of group-trip friction is not money itself but a silent mismatch in what people expected to spend. Agreeing the tier in advance, with the itinerary and a running expense log in one place — which is what **Trypinn** does — turns an awkward conversation at the end into a five-minute one at the start.
